mechanism_narrative: The level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is negatively correlated with 20-day forward S&P 500 returns; lower rates compress discount rates on equity cash flows, leading to positive returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC of FEDFUNDS level with 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.5%, it signals an easing monetary policy that compresses discount rates, producing positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% occurs in more than 40% of 20-day return periods, but positive returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 135,000 thousand persons and unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 7.0%, it indicates a strong labor market that supports economic expansion and positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The condition PAYEMS > 135000 and UNRATE < 7.0 occurs in more than 40% of 20-day return periods, but positive returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months), higher federal funds rates predict negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns due to reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: The condition FEDFUNDS > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months occurs in more than 40% of 20-day return periods, but negative returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate (UNRATE) is negatively correlated with 20-day forward S&P 500 returns; lower unemployment rates indicate a stronger labor market that supports economic growth and positive equity returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC of UNRATE with 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The industrial production index (INDPRO) is positively correlated with 60-day forward S&P 500 returns; higher industrial output signals robust economic activity that supports equity market performance.
failure_condition: Rank IC of INDPRO with 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Residential investment (RSAFS) is positively correlated with 5-day forward S&P 500 returns; higher residential investment indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to short-term positive equity returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC of RSAFS with 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 850 thousand units, it signals strong demand and positive 5-day forward S&P 500 returns; robust housing activity indicates expanding consumer demand and economic growth.
failure_condition: HOUST > 850 occurs in more than 40% of 5-day return periods, but positive returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p>0.05).
